blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: Jeremiah uses siege, wound, tears, maternal bodies, non-burial, creation undone, imprisonment, displacement, and fractured memory to represent catastrophe and survival. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. Interpretations differ on some details.

A literary feature to notice is that The received book combines poetry, prose sermons, narratives, letters, headings, repeated accounts, restoration collections, nation oracles, and an appendix produced through a long compositional and textual history. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. The evidence leaves some details unresolved.
